checkpoints.description: [1/1] fix the comparison-branch lowering so a left operand held in a temporary register is the one compared, then pin it with a runtime test and a shape test and record the ADR

impact_assessment.why: a miscompile: _emit_comparison_branch calls _emit_left_operand then always compares rcx, but _emit_left_operand puts a non-leaf right operand's left value in a temporary and sets left_hold, so the branch compared a stale rcx (if t > (i & 65535) with t negative took the true branch; the value form of the same compare was correct)
impact_assessment.benefits: correct control flow for every if/while whose comparison has a non-leaf right operand and a non-leaf left operand; the value-form and branch-form lowerings then agree
impact_assessment.risks: contract: generated bytes change only at such compares; dependency: none; concurrency: cairn tree is clean and no other task is active; state: ledger only
impact_assessment.mitigation: honour left_hold exactly as _emit_binary already does, pin the shape and the runtime answer, run the full suite and the benchmark diff

checkpoints.description: [1/1] committed as cceebbd: _emit_comparison_branch now consumes self.left_hold and clears it before cmp, falling back to rcx, so a left value parked in a temporary by a non-leaf right operand is the one branched on; failing-first proof on HEAD showed all three new tests failing (end-to-end 1/4/5 against the correct 2/3/0), with all three passing after the fix; full suite 1366 OK; 5/5 project gates passed; ADR-090 records the fix and the two G-004 benchmark runs that read +9.6 to +613 percent under host contention (compile times ~10x, short cases worst) with the clean 17a5e10 baseline restored and the loaded logs kept outside the tree; no speed claim; checklists: passed
Task 'cairn-branch-hold' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/1] replace the power-of-two divides in print_hex (16) and print_char (256) with mask and logical shift, pin the emitted shape with failing-first runtime tests, prove the output is byte-identical and the paired A/B is faster, record the ADR and G-004 benchmark diff

impact_assessment.why: print_hex peeled eleven nibbles with eleven serial div r64 instructions and print_char paid one div just to isolate a byte; hex_io is the largest remaining real loss to C++ and the benchmark source records this as the next optimisation
impact_assessment.benefits: the serial divide chain leaves the value path; hex_io best time measured 66.08 to 52.96 ms (-19.9 percent) in a paired interleaved A/B with an identical full checksum
impact_assessment.risks: contract: unsigned 64-bit output must stay byte-identical; dependency: shift_imm already emits C1 /5 for shr, no new instruction; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first shape tests, existing end-to-end and cross-language twin parity tests, a full suite run, and a paired A/B with identical checksums

impact_assessment.why: a paired A/B on a contended host confirmed str_scan is a real loss (1.18x C, 1.23x C++) and its inlined byte load still pays a NUL test and miss constant that a str_len guard proves unreachable
impact_assessment.benefits: the scan inner loop drops two instructions per byte; paired A/B with a +1.3 percent identical-binary control measured -10.3 percent best
impact_assessment.risks: contract: str_byte(s, len) must still answer -1; dependency: no new instruction, reuses movzx_load8_sib; concurrency: none; state: facts are scoped to the guarded loop body
impact_assessment.mitigation: only a strict '<' guard with a proven non-negative index earns the fact, facts are invalidated on reassignment and restored at loop exit, and tests pin the inclusive and unguarded refusals plus the terminator read after the loop

checkpoints.description: [1/1] rotate the read_char scan so the EOF guard is the loop's conditional back-edge and the body falls through into the next fetch, removing the unconditional jump; failing-first shape and refusal tests, paired A/B with identical-binary control, ADR, full suite and gates

impact_assessment.why: char_stream is a confirmed 1.19x-C loss and its generic lowering fetched at the top then ended in an unconditional jump, while gcc's getchar loop uses a conditional back-edge
impact_assessment.benefits: the per-byte unconditional jump disappears; a paired A/B with a -0.1 percent control measured -4.8 percent best with byte-identical 4 MiB output
impact_assessment.risks: contract: EOF must still exit with the same checksum; dependency: reuses the promoted read_char inline with a caller-supplied join label; concurrency: none; state: no new static state
impact_assessment.mitigation: match only the exact three-statement while-true scan shape, keep one fetch site, refuse when the accumulator is not a register home, add a refusal test for a non-scan loop, and verify the four-language twin parity
